The Government's case is that the suit land is a fishery, locally known as Magura beel fishery, and it was recorded in the khatian of the Deputy Commissioner under section 20(3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as a non-retainable khas land and that the Government has been possessing the same since acquisition. 

 7. In revision the High Court Division restored the judgment and decree of the trial Court With regard to the plaintiffs' document Ext. 6 which the appellate Court did not at all consider the High. Court Division held that the khatian did not support the plaintiffs case as stated in para 2 of the plaint, that 14 annas 8 gondas and 2 karas and 2 kranti share of the suit land belonged to one Ram Proshad Chakraborty and the remaining 1 anna 1 gonda 1 kara and 1 kranti share belonged to Abdul Wazid and 5 others in khasmaliki right. From Khatian No. 675, filed by the plaintiffs and marked as Ext. 6, the High Court Division held that 120 acres and 40 decimals of land, recorded in that khatian, belonged to Ram Proshad Sarma and Ram Hory Chakraborty in 6-1/3 shares each and the remaining 1/3rd to Gagan Chakraborty, Girish Chakraborty and Norendra Chandra Chakraborty sons of the Gopinath Chabraborty, in equal 1/3rd share. The names of Abdul Wazid and his alleged other co-sharers were nowhere found in that khatian. Suit Plot No. 2934 was found to be recorded as petit land in Ext. 6.
